column1: # The port ledger: every Python file in the RUNTIME SURFACE - `tools/`, `serve/`, `chat.py`, `setup.py` - and what
# This is the machine-readable answer to "what has been ported, and what holds it".  docs/CXX_PORT.md is the
# narrative; this is the list a script can read.  A port is not done until the row has a TEST: the acceptance is
# the reference's own output, so a row without one is a claim rather than a fact.
#   status = ported      the C++ is verified against the reference's own bytes or stdout
#            not-a-target the behaviour already exists in C++, or the file IS the reference
#            needs-surface a port needs a subsystem this tree does not have (named in the note)
#            out-of-scope  the repository's own docs/CXX_PORT.md places it outside "where possible"
# DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE OF THIS LIST, so that the sentence above is true rather than approximately true:
# `bench/` (historical benchmark results and their one-off scripts), `sycl/` (the Intel port's own tree),
# `ref/`, `docs/media/`, and the vendored `third_party/`.  What this lists is the surface the engine ships.
